1. Science. 2006 Sep 8;313(5792):1402. doi: 10.1126/science.1130197.

Detecting awareness in the vegetative state.

Owen AM(1), Coleman MR, Boly M, Davis MH, Laureys S, Pickard JD.

Author information:
(1)Medical Research Council Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit, Cambridge CB2 
2EF, UK. adrian.owen@mrc-cbu.cam.ac.uk

Comment in
    Science. 2006 Sep 8;313(5792):1376-9. doi: 10.1126/science.313.5792.1376.
    Science. 2006 Sep 8;313(5792):1395-6. doi: 10.1126/science.1132881.
    Science. 2007 Mar 2;315(5816):1221; author reply 1221. doi: 
10.1126/science.1135096.
    Science. 2007 Mar 2;315(5816):1221; author reply 1221. doi: 
10.1126/science.1135284.

We used functional magnetic resonance imaging to demonstrate preserved conscious 
awareness in a patient fulfilling the criteria for a diagnosis of vegetative 
state. When asked to imagine playing tennis or moving around her home, the 
patient activated predicted cortical areas in a manner indistinguishable from 
that of healthy volunteers.
